proof_text:
We evaluate the statements under all four assignments of truth values
to $P$ and $Q$:

1. If both $P$ and $Q$ are true, then $\htmlData{mlg-ref=5c2e616e642e2f}{P \land Q}$ is true, so
   $\htmlData{mlg-ref=5c6e6f74}{\neg \left(\htmlData{mlg-ref=5c2e616e642e2f}{P \land Q}\right)}$ is false. Meanwhile, $\htmlData{mlg-ref=5c6e6f74}{\neg P}$ and
   $\htmlData{mlg-ref=5c6e6f74}{\neg Q}$ are both false, so $\htmlData{mlg-ref=5c2e6f722e2f}{\htmlData{mlg-ref=5c6e6f74}{\neg P} \lor \htmlData{mlg-ref=5c6e6f74}{\neg Q}}$ is false.
   Both sides agree.

2. If at least one of $P$ or $Q$ is false, then $\htmlData{mlg-ref=5c2e616e642e2f}{P \land Q}$ is
   false, so $\htmlData{mlg-ref=5c6e6f74}{\neg \left(\htmlData{mlg-ref=5c2e616e642e2f}{P \land Q}\right)}$ is true. At the same time, at least
   one of $\htmlData{mlg-ref=5c6e6f74}{\neg P}$ or $\htmlData{mlg-ref=5c6e6f74}{\neg Q}$ is true, so
   $\htmlData{mlg-ref=5c2e6f722e2f}{\htmlData{mlg-ref=5c6e6f74}{\neg P} \lor \htmlData{mlg-ref=5c6e6f74}{\neg Q}}$ is true. Again, both sides agree.

The dual identity
$\htmlData{mlg-ref=5c2e6966662e2f}{\htmlData{mlg-ref=5c6e6f74}{\neg \left(\htmlData{mlg-ref=5c2e6f722e2f}{P \lor Q}\right)} \iff \left(\htmlData{mlg-ref=5c2e616e642e2f}{\htmlData{mlg-ref=5c6e6f74}{\neg P} \land \htmlData{mlg-ref=5c6e6f74}{\neg Q}}\right)}$ follows by
applying the first identity to $\htmlData{mlg-ref=5c6e6f74}{\neg P}$ and $\htmlData{mlg-ref=5c6e6f74}{\neg Q}$ together
with the law of double negation.

Proof: """We evaluate the statements under all four assignments of truth values
          to {.P.} and {.Q.}:

          1. If both {.P.} and {.Q.} are true, then {.P \.and./ Q.} is true, so
             {.\not{P \.and./ Q}.} is false. Meanwhile, {.\not{P}.} and
             {.\not{Q}.} are both false, so {.\not{P} \.or./ \not{Q}.} is false.
             Both sides agree.

          2. If at least one of {.P.} or {.Q.} is false, then {.P \.and./ Q.} is
             false, so {.\not{P \.and./ Q}.} is true. At the same time, at least
             one of {.\not{P}.} or {.\not{Q}.} is true, so
             {.\not{P} \.or./ \not{Q}.} is true. Again, both sides agree.

          The dual identity
          {.\not{P \.or./ Q} \.iff./ (\not{P} \.and./ \not{Q}).} follows by
          applying the first identity to {.\not{P}.} and {.\not{Q}.} together
          with the law of double negation."""
